scope.summary: Implement conform-wardrobe batch per Section 13.24 (SREQ-014, BodySlide batch-build pattern): a one-call operation that refits an entire outfit library to a target body as parallel Handshake jobs with leases, backpressure, and per-garment result receipts.
acceptance_criteria: conform_wardrobe(body_id, garment_ids[]) enqueues one refit job per garment (fit-space interpolation where samples exist, grow-into-garment otherwise) under the scheduler with leases and backpressure; parallel lanes do not contend on the same garment row.
Each garment resolves to a typed per-item result (FIT | FAILED with reason) plus receipt; the batch result row aggregates counts and is machine-readable.

Cancelling the batch stops pending jobs, lets in-flight jobs finish or roll back cleanly, and marks the batch PARTIAL with an accurate per-item ledger; re-running resumes only unfinished items (idempotent).
Batch progress and per-item states are observable via RUNTIME status/TraceProjection without polling the individual jobs.
scope.risk_if_missed: Dressing a new body means manually refitting garments one by one — the exact workflow tax that makes Daz character swaps miserable — and agent swarms cannot batch-produce dressed character variations.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit, Cloth, and contact integration

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Reconcile the BodyKit cloth bridge with shared topology/material/collider snapshots, the per-tier interaction matrix, portal-aware cavity metadata, final f64 authority, and promotion-safe receipts without expanding BodyKit anatomy authoring in this slice.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.

Use authenticated SurrealDB record-user table/field PERMISSIONS intersected with ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; administrative/root credentials and UI filtering are never the security boundary. PostgreSQL and SQLite access paths are forbidden.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
